Explicit recordA/B/C anchors independently identify the three iri focuses; blank names are local graph identities, not interchangeable wildcards. Every SELECT solution yields one SPARQL constraint result with its current focus/value, named source constraint and source shape.

The Recommendation forbids every explicit VALUES and requires nested projections to return potentially-prebound variables except its two optional context variables. The dated draft forbids only VALUES mentioning potentially-prebound variables and removes that projection rule. Both forbid MINUS and AS assigning this. The draft SERVICE refusal is PurRDF implementation policy under the draft SHOULD/MUST refusal rule; it is not a universal draft prohibition.

extensions.processorPolicy: PurRDF refuses SERVICE under the dated draft; the draft permits a processor that admits it, so this case grades a declared PurRDF policy rather than a universal draft requirement

cases.rationale: The SELECT has one solution whose failure binding is true. The SHACL SPARQL validator must report a semantic processor failure; producing a normal nonconformance report, a file error or a runner crash does not satisfy this contract.

The single solution binds message to "row message". The ordered SPARQL report mapping chooses this binding before the constraint declaration. The expected result therefore requires row message and does not require the lower-priority declared message.

Both targets are distinct RDF 1.2 triple terms. The matched about object must equal the complete focus triple term before the OPTIONAL runs. Only recordGood has p; the expected sole result carries the bad triple term exactly as focus and value.

The sequence ex:p followed by inverse ex:q reaches z from a through m, but reaches no node from b. Exactly b violates minCount 1. The result path must encode this sequence/inverse topology; a blank wildcard, reversed sequence or alternative-path structure cannot satisfy it. MinCount does not require a value.

Attached rules prebind this to each target. Only b,c lack p, so exactly b missing true and c missing true are inferred. Existing input triples are not counted as new inferences; no a missing triple is permitted.
